I am trying to run multi-species occupancy models using unmarked.

I also can't really interpret the garbled output. If you are getting very high estimate and SE values, I would not trust those results. I'd agree with both you and Marc that the most likely explanation is that the model is just too complicated for the dataset.

A few ideas:
- Fewer covariates
- Estimate only the pairwise interactions (i.e., set maxOrder to 2) and hold the higher-order interactions to 0.
- Reduce the number of species in the model, if you can do so and still meet your research goals

Sometimes you can use penalized likelihood to help with this situation. See the occuMulti vignette, sections 5 and 6 (and the cited paper) for an overview:

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/unmarked/vignettes/occuMulti.html#model-fitting-challenges

Ken

I also can't really interpret the garbled output. If you are getting very high estimate and SE values, I would not trust those results. I'd agree with both you and Marc that the most likely explanation is that the model is just too complicated for the dataset.

A few ideas:
- Fewer covariates
- Estimate only the pairwise interactions (i.e., set maxOrder to 2) and hold the higher-order interactions to 0.
- Reduce the number of species in the model, if you can do so and still meet your research goals

Sometimes you can use penalized likelihood to help with this situation. See the occuMulti vignette, sections 5 and 6 (and the cited paper) for an overview:

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/unmarked/vignettes/occuMulti.html#model-fitting-challenges

Ken
